newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, Bahrain to hold reconciliation talks.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Bahrain to hold reconciliation talks.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Bahrain and Qatar, their countries embroiled in a border dispute, are expected to meet in Riyadh on Tuesday to discuss ways to improve ties, Gulf diplomats said on Sunday.
The meeting will be held under the auspices of a committee formed by the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in Doha in December to try to solve the border row, they added.
The four-nation team is headed by Saudi Arabia and includes the remaining GCC members -- Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates.
"The upcoming meeting will try to clear the atmosphere of misunderstanding and mistrust between the two neighbours and pave the way for normal relations between them", said one Gulf diplomat.
"It will bring the foreign ministers of the two states face to face and encourage dialogue between them, but it will not seek to draft a formula to resolve the border row", he added.
The committee was scheduled to hold its first meeting in Cairo late last month on the sidelines of a conference of the eight allies of the Damascus Declaration -- the GCC states, Syria and Egypt.
But it was rescheduled at Saudi request for Tuesday.
The eight nations formed their alliance after uniting behind the U.S.-led 1991 offensive to drive Iraqi forces from Kuwait.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked in a decades-old territorial dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice at The Hague, a move bitterly opposed by Bahrain which insists on an Arab solution.

Ties further worsened after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying and boycotted the December 7-9 GCC summit in Doha to protest against Qatar's refusal to withdraw the border dispute from international arbitration.
Bahrain last month pardoned the two Qataris after a state security court sentenced them to three years in jail and fined them 1,000 dinars ($2,652) each for spying for Qatar.
